validity.recommendation: No action on existence/classification/duplicate axes. See the separate spec-concern entry below for Length.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real and currently operating. Three independent origins name this specific pipeline, not a GEM-only entity: (1) Intergas Central Asia's own official 'Общая информация' page (intergas.kz) lists 'МГ «Газли-Шымкент»' by name among the trunk lines it currently operates under UMG Shymkent; (2) informburo.kz, an independent Kazakh news outlet, reported a July-2019 accident/fire specifically 'на магистральном газопроводе Газли-Шымкент' at the 76th km (in Bukhara, Uzbekistan), sourced to a statement from Uztransgaz (the Uzbek gas company) -- an operator/press pairing wholly independent of Intergas; (3) neftegaz.ru (Russian trade press, 2022) names a real, physical gas-metering station, GIS Shardara, sited '​на 314м км МГП Газли - Шымкент.' All three are consistent and none traces to GEM. CLASSIFICATION: correct. All three sources call it a 'магистральный газопровод'/'МГП' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline) carrying natural gas -- Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both well supported, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's other Uzbekistan-origin Bukhara/Gazli-area lines, principally Bukhara-Tashkent-Bishkek-Almaty (BGR-TBA, P0739/P5810). Intergas's own general-info page lists 'МГ «Бухарский Газоносный Район – Ташкент-Бишкек-Алматы»' and 'МГ «Газли-Шымкент»' as two SEPARATE named pipelines under the same UMG Shymkent division, and the neftegaz.ru article independently corroborates the same split in one article (GIS Shardara on 'МГП Газли-Шымкент' vs. GIS Zhetysay on 'МГП Бухарский газоносный район - Ташкент - Бишкек - Алматы'). So P3956 is a genuinely distinct physical system sharing only a common origin region with BGR-TBA, not a relabel or double-count of it. ATTRIBUTION caveat (not raised to a full concern): gem.wiki's own infobox records this line's Owner as joint 'Qazaqgaz, Uztransgaz' -- consistent with informburo.kz's report that the July-2019 accident (at km 76, on Uzbek territory) was announced by Uztransgaz, i.e. the Uzbek state gas company plausibly operates/owns the Uzbekistan-territory segment. GEM's sheet records Owner1=QazaqGaz at 100%, with no Uzbek co-owner. This mirrors the convention already used elsewhere in the Kazakhstan-gas roster for other Uzbekistan-origin lines (P0739/P2289/P5695/P5810 all record only the Kazakh-side operator too), so this is flagged for awareness rather than as a row-specific defect.

validity.recommendation: Re-derive Length from a source that reports Gazli-Shymkent's OWN point-to-point length, not the combined KMG system total. Do not treat 877.00 km as sourced. If no independent per-line figure turns up, note it as unresolved rather than leaving the current (likely overstated) citation trail implied by gem.wiki.
validity.researcher_notes: LengthKnown=877.00 km traces (via gem.wiki's own citation, read for leads only -- never cited per standing rule 1) to the KMG Annual Report 2020 PDF, downloaded and read with pdftotext -layout. That report's 'TRUNK PIPELINE GAS TRANSPORTATION' table gives only ONE combined row: 'BGR-TBA, Gazli-Shymkent | 2,462 km | 10.2 bln m3/year' -- it does NOT break the two pipelines out individually. 877 km is exactly 2,462 minus 1,585 (GEM's own P0739 BGR-TBA length), i.e. an arithmetic residual/inferred split from the combined total, not an independently reported per-line figure -- the source cited for 'Length: 877 km' on gem.wiki does not actually state 877 km anywhere. Two further, independent signals both point to a materially SHORTER true length: (a) GEM's own drawn route geometry for P3956 (a 4-vertex LineString in the routes repo, data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P3956.geojson) sums to 574.4 km by great-circle segment distance; (b) the straight-line geodesic distance between the two endpoint coordinates used on gem.wiki's own embedded map for this page (Gazli 40.12745N/63.4567E to Shymkent 42.34168N/69.5901E) is 568.7 km -- almost identical to the drawn route, meaning the existing route is essentially a direct line between those two points, leaving no plausible detour that would add ~300 km. So three converging observations (an unsupported combined-total citation, GEM's own drawn route, and the raw endpoint geometry) all point toward the recorded 877 km overstating the line by roughly 300 km (about 53%), with a more probable true length in the 570-650 km range. I could not find an independent, non-GEM, per-line length figure to propose as a replacement (informburo.kz's '76th km' marker and neftegaz.ru's '314th km' marker for GIS Shardara are consistent with a line in the several-hundred-km range but do not themselves state a total). Diameter (1220 mm), Capacity (4.3 bcm/y) and StartYear1 (1988) have the SAME underlying problem -- gem.wiki's citations for these either point to the same unresolved combined-total source or to intergas.kz/ru/reports/88, which is a live but content-ROTATING reports-index page (currently shows 2025-2026 filings, not a fixed link to the cited 2019/2020 annual report) -- so none of the three could be independently corroborated in this pass either; see the paired UNRESOLVED fills below rather than treating them as sourced.

fills.researcher_notes: Intergas Central Asia lists this line among those it currently operates. The July-2019 accident report (personnel actively repairing an active line) is present-tense operating evidence even though the literal word 'operating' does not appear -- status is inferable per convention.
Trivial, uncontested -- both sources call it a 'газопровод' (gas pipeline) throughout.
Both sources classify it as 'магистральный газопровод'/'МГП' (trunk/main gas pipeline) -- consistent with transmission, not a gathering or feeder line.

Inferential, single strong source: the pipeline is named for and grouped (on Intergas's own site) with the Bukhara/Gazli gas-bearing region system that feeds South Kazakhstan. No source found that states in so many words 'sourced from the Gazli field', hence tier=medium rather than high.

informburo.kz confirms the Uzbekistan-territory end (accident 'в Бухаре' at km 76); neftegaz.ru confirms a Kazakhstan-territory facility (GIS Shardara) at km 314 along the same named line, en route to Shymkent. StartPrefecture/District and StartState/Province were left blank in the worklist and are NOT filled here -- I could not independently confirm whether Gazli town itself sits in Bukhara or Navoiy region of Uzbekistan without a source I could verify, so left as-is rather than guess.

Both pages are the operator's own site (RU and EN editions of the same corporate 'about' content), so this is really one origin, not two independent ones -- marked independent=false accordingly, tier still high because it is a direct first-party operational statement naming this exact pipeline among the lines Intergas Central Asia runs.

intergas.kz's own English 'About the company' page states in so many words that 'Intergas Central Asia, JSC is a subsidiary of the National Company QazaqGaz, JSC.' kase.kz (Kazakhstan Stock Exchange, an independent regulatory-market source) independently lists QazaqGaz (KZTG) as the national gas holding company, corroborating the parent-company relationship from outside Intergas itself. Note: this only supports the KAZAKH-side ownership at 100%; see the paired validity note above re: an unaddressed possible Uztransgaz co-ownership of the Uzbekistan-territory segment, which this pass does not resolve.

summary: P3956 Gazli-Shymkent: existence/classification/duplicate all CONFIRMED (high) via Intergas's own operator listing + an independent 2019 accident report + independent trade press naming a real km-314 station on this line -- and it is demonstrably NOT the same pipeline as BGR-TBA (P0739/P5810) despite the shared Uzbekistan origin region. One material CONCERN: Length=877.00 km is an unsupported arithmetic residual from a KMG combined-system total (2,462 km for BGR-TBA+Gazli-Shymkent together), and both GEM's own drawn route (574.4 km) and the raw endpoint geodesic distance (568.7 km) point to a true length closer to ~570-650 km -- flag for correction. Status/Fuel/PipelineType/FuelSource/Location/Operator/Owner refs ADDED (mostly high tier); Diameter/Capacity/StartYear1 left UNRESOLVED, no independent source found.
